source.title: Mechanistic Analysis of Safety Disparities Across Vision and Text Modalities in Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Imran Kutianawala; Sarthak Tayal; Melissa Yu; Ayda Sultan

page_placements.theme: Cross-modality: text-derived refusal direction applied to image, video, audio and VLA inputs

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Uses difference-in-means refusal vectors and tests activation ablation and addition against refusal rates, applying the original method in vision-language models.
record.gate_note: The steering experiments intervene at one selected layer (17 in Gemma-3-4B-it; 34 in Gemma-3-27B-it), at the final token position during prompt processing and generation, rather than ablating the direction at every layer and position. General capability preservation is not evaluated. The paper also reports SAE feature counts and overlap; those findings concern safety-related features rather than the refusal direction or refusal behavior directly.
record.test_reason: Applies the difference-in-means refusal direction to Gemma-3 vision-language models (4B, 27B). It subtracts and adds the vector at one layer and measures refusal rates on harmful and safe text and image inputs. This is a new setting (VLMs, image inputs) with a close but modified intervention: additive steering with a non-normalized vector at one layer, not projection ablation at all layers.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors find text and image refusal directions geometrically aligned, but harmful images project more weakly onto the direction and fire fewer safety SAE features. Text-derived vectors steer image refusal much more strongly than the reverse, an asymmetry that is smaller in 27B. They call the analysis largely correlational and recommend vision-specific safety fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the original difference-in-means construction and tests ablation/addition, but evaluates Gemma VLMs with selected single-layer interventions at the final token position rather than ablating the direction across all layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: Intervention layer and coefficient were selected using a held-out set of 10 samples per data type. The selected layer was 17 for Gemma-3-4B-it and 34 for Gemma-3-27B-it. Results vary by vector source, target modality, and model size. The authors also note that the judging model is non-deterministic.

fits_no_version.finding: Text- and image-derived difference-in-means refusal directions peak at cosine 0.941 (4B, layer 14) and 0.958 (27B, layer 23). Harmful images project only 0.62 and 0.64 as strongly as text onto the text direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In VLMs, image and text refusal directions are geometrically aligned, but harmful images engage the shared direction more weakly than harmful text.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful images are refused far less than semantically identical harmful text (4B: 24.0% vs 89.5%; 27B: 64.5% vs 83.0%). A safe image lowers text refusal in 4B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: VLMs refuse harmful requests less when the request is delivered as an image than as text.

fits_no_version.finding: Decoded safety SAE features fire far less often on harmful image inputs than on matched text inputs (e.g., feature 21: 0 vs 117 rows).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful image inputs activate fewer safety-relevant SAE features than semantically matched text in Gemma-3-4B-it.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-modal steering is asymmetric: text-derived vectors transfer to images strongly, image-derived vectors transfer to text weakly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A refusal direction derived from text transfers to image inputs in VLMs more strongly than the reverse.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code will be released upon publication
record.problems: The authors describe much of the analysis as correlational and say it does not establish which representation differences causally drive the modality gap. The steering test uses a selected single layer, not all layers. General capabilities are not evaluated. Refusal judgments use Gemini-2.5-Flash, which the authors say is non-deterministic.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports raw SAE Jaccard-overlap layer/probe settings and an NSFW URL SAE appendix. These feature-overlap results do not measure refusal rates or the refusal direction directly; the decoded FigStep feature counts most directly related to the authors' safety-feature explanation are included above.

untested.parts: Preservation of general abilities is not evaluated. Directional ablation by projection at every layer and position is not used: steering is additive, at one layer and the final token. Text-vector injection on safe text and image-vector injection on safe images are not run.
Jailbreak mechanism via suppression of the direction and adversarial training are not tested.
Harmfulness is not separated from refusal.
Languages, model variants and base-to-instruct transfer are not tested. Cross-modal transfer is studied but is not among V6's named axes.

record.verdict_notes: The 'ablation' is h <- h + αv with a non-normalized difference-in-means vector at a single layer (17 for 4B, 34 for 27B), applied at the final token during prefill and decode. It is not orthogonal projection at all layers as in Arditi et al., so V1 support rests on activation subtraction. Layer and coefficient were tuned on 10 samples. Baselines vary across experiments because the Gemini judge is non-deterministic. Image-side baselines are low in 4B (9.6%, 12.5%), so near-total removal there is a small absolute change. There is no capability evaluation. Cross-modal transfer is not a named V6 axis, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate the direction at every layer and position, and does not test whether general abilities are largely preserved.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Does not test affine or cone representations, or whether additional refusal directions contribute beyond the measured direction.
Does not separate harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
Does not test transfer across languages, reuse of a direction across model variants, or transfer from base to instruct models.
Does not vary when or how refusal training is performed.

relationships.condition: Gemma-3-4B-it and Gemma-3-27B-it VLMs: text-derived vector interventions, plus same-modality image-derived ablation (single-layer additive steering)
relationships.reason: Subtracting the vector removed most refusal and adding it induced near-total refusal on safe images (ST-27B-T-HARM, ST-27B-T-IMAGE, ST-27B-T-SAFEIMAGE, ST-4B-T-IMAGE, ST-4B-T-SAFEIMAGE, ST-4B-I-HARM, ST-27B-I-HARM).
relationships.display_finding: Subtracting the vector removed most refusal, while adding it induced near-total refusal on safe images.

relation.reason: It measures refusal and compliance rates after subtracting or adding DIM refusal vectors, for same-modality and cross-modal inputs (Tables 3 and 6).

tranche.reason: New setting (Gemma-3 VLMs, image inputs) with refusal-rate results under DIM-direction subtraction and addition. The intervention departs from the original: single-layer additive steering of a non-normalized vector at the final token, not projection at all layers and positions. So it is not T1.

source_check.notes: The pack shows no [lN] ids, so verdicts are numbered l1 and l2 in listed order. The study is a COLM 2026 submission under review (year 2026). Its 'ablation' adds alpha times a non-normalized DIM vector at one layer (17 for 4B, 34 for 27B), final token only; it is not projection removal. There is no random-direction control and no capability benchmark, only degeneracy rates. Baseline refusal differs across experiments (FigStep images 24.0% in Table 1 vs 9.6%/12.5% in Table 3); the authors attribute this to a non-deterministic judge.

statements.correction: This study: single LM residual layer, layer 17 (Gemma-3-4B-it, alpha -1.5) and layer 34 (Gemma-3-27B-it, alpha -2.0). Additive subtraction of a non-normalized image-derived harmful-minus-safe DIM vector at the final token position (prefill and decode). Harmful text from AdvBench. Gemini-2.5-Flash judge. 27B: 93.6% -> 21.8%.
statements.problem: The 96.2%->73.8% figure (Gemma-3-4B-it, image-derived vector on harmful text) is right. But the group's conditions don't describe this study: its layers are not '12, 27', and its cited direction is image-derived DIM, not 'text-derived'.

statements.correction: Minor precision: 0.62/0.64 are ratios of peak vision to peak text scalar projection, using held-out harmful minus safe activations (G-F, H-E) on the text direction. The refusal comparison is FigStep images vs their plain-text versions (conditions B vs C, n=200).

reader_labels.reason: Ablation sharply reduced harmful-input refusal and addition made safe inputs refuse in these tested settings (ST-4B-T-IMAGE, ST-4B-T-SAFEIMAGE, ST-4B-I-HARM, ST-27B-T-HARM, ST-27B-T-IMAGE, ST-27B-T-SAFEIMAGE, ST-27B-I-HARM).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Ablation of harmful text with the 4B text-derived vector and cross-modal text steering with image-derived vectors
reader_labels.reason: Refusal remained at 14.0% after the 4B text ablation and at 73.8% and 21.8% after image-vector ablation of harmful text; image-vector additions induced only 7.2% and 40.8% refusal on safe text (ST-4B-T-HARM, ST-4B-I-TEXT, ST-4B-I-SAFETEXT, ST-27B-I-TEXT, ST-27B-I-SAFETEXT).
